newsitem.title: USA: UAL chairman sees favorable '97 results.
newsitem.headline: UAL chairman sees favorable '97 results.

text.p: UAL Corp, parent of United Airlines, expects 1997 to be an even better year for the company than 1996, chairman and chief executive officer Gerald Greenwald said in remarks prepared for delivery to the Society of Airline Analysts.
"We expect 1997 to be an even better year for United than 1996 has been," Greenwald said.

"With one of the best U.S. domestic capacity environments the industry has seen in years, and with our expectation that United's domestic unit revenue growth will surpass that of the industry, we are looking forward to another year of excellent results," Greenwald noted.

The executive also discussed the company's three key objectives for the coming year: to improve the company's pretax margin ranking, on-time departure performance and customer preference for United, particularly among high-yield customers.
